screens.prompt: In B5, total Q1 revenue for all three regions with one function.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close every bracket: =SUM(B2:B4).
hints.func-sum: Add the three cells with SUM instead of typing 1200+1450+930.
hints.require-ref: Your answer has to point at the Q1 cells, not repeat a total you worked out yourself.
hints.value: Close, but that is not the Q1 total. Check that the range covers all three regions and none of the Q2 column.
hints.error: SUM only fails on what you feed it: #VALUE! means a cell in the range holds text instead of a number, #REF! means the range was pointed at something deleted. Re-select B2:B4 and let Excel write the range for you.
hints.hardcoded: Your total only works for the numbers in front of you, which means a figure is typed in. Sum the whole range, B2:B4, so a corrected region lands in the total on its own.

reject.why: adds the cells by hand instead of using SUM
the right cells, the wrong function
range stops one row short, so West is missing
picks up the Q2 column as well as Q1
types the numbers into SUM instead of pointing at B2:B4
the total is right, then it is divided by zero
adds West as a typed number, so a corrected B4 never reaches the total

variants.why: North is revised up to 1300, so the total has to move with it
South is corrected to 1500, which is the change the docs describe
West drops to 1000, so a formula that stopped at B3 would miss it

docs.explain:
SUM adds the numbers in the range you give it. Any text or blank cell inside that range is stepped over rather than counted. =SUM(B2:B4) covers 1200, 1450 and 930 and returns 3580. Change South to 1500 and the total follows.

The failure runs the other way. A number stored as text looks like a number and is skipped without a warning, so the total comes out low and nothing on screen says why. A region missing from a total is usually a left-aligned figure in the column.

Point at the range rather than at three cells. 1200+1450+930 breaks when a row is inserted, while B2:B4 grows to take the new row in.

errors.text: A cell in the range holds text where SUM expected a number, usually the heading or the Region column in place of the Q1 figures.
The function name is misspelled as SUMM or SU. Excel reads what is there and does not guess at the rest.
SUM(B2:B5) would reach the label in B5 as well. A range that runs one cell long is how a total quietly doubles itself.

docs.atWork: Every monthly close: one row per branch, one column per period, and a total at the bottom that updates itself.
docs.outcome: Total a column with one function instead of typing every cell.

seo.title: SUM in Excel: total a column in one cell
seo.description: SUM adds a whole range in one cell. This exercise totals 3580 from three rows, then shows why a number stored as text never reaches the total.
